svg.text: Vertical-axis turbine, three blade – side elevation and plan
120° between blades – wider spacing than the tulip
direct vertical shaft – no bevel drive
INDICATIVE ARTIST'S ILLUSTRATION – NOT TO SCALE
Dimensions to be confirmed by survey and detailed design
Commercially available three-blade vertical-axis turbine, but up-graded from wind duty for heavy-duty use in water.
Rotor: 1 800 mm swept diameter x 2 400 mm high. 3 no. twisted blades carried on radial arms from a central hub column, 105° of twist over the height.
Same family as the 'tulip' on Drawing 8, but with three blades set much further apart and a near-cylindrical sweep rather than an egg profile.
The open sweep passes debris and fish more readily than a close-packed rotor, at the cost of a lower solidity and a higher running speed.
Vertical axis: a straight shaft runs to the pod above, with no bevel drive. Upper thrust and lower guide bearings, both water lubricated.
Shown against a plain background for identification only. Sizes are indicative and to be confirmed by the supplier.
